title: Playing with Numbers
description: Class 8 IMO — Playing with numbers: the generalised form of numbers, divisibility tests using the general form, and number puzzles like reverse-and-subtract and cryptarithmetic.

topics.title: Generalised Form of Numbers
topics.concept: A two-digit number with tens digit a and units digit b is written ab = 10a + b. For example, 34 = 10 × 3 + 4. Reversing the digits gives ba = 10b + a.

examples.problem: Write the reverse of 'ab' in generalised form.

topics.title: Divisibility Tests
topics.concept: Using the general form, a number is divisible by 3 or 9 when its digit sum is, and by 11 when the alternating digit sum is 0 or a multiple of 11. A number is divisible by 2 when it ends in an even digit.

examples.solution: Digit sum 1 + 2 + 3 = 6, which is divisible by 3, so yes.

examples.problem: When is a number divisible by 9?
examples.solution: When its digit sum is divisible by 9.

recap: Divisible by 3/9: check the digit sum.
Divisible by 11: check the alternating digit sum.

quiz.explanation: Digit sum 2 + 0 + 7 = 9, divisible by 9, so yes.

topics.title: Number Puzzles
topics.concept: The difference of a two-digit number and its reverse is ab − ba = 9(a − b), always a multiple of 9. Their sum is ab + ba = 11(a + b), always a multiple of 11. So 52 − 25 = 27 = 9 × 3.
recap: ab − ba = 9(a − b); ab + ba = 11(a + b).
Reverse-and-subtract always gives a multiple of 9.

questions.q: ab − ba is always divisible by ___ ?
questions.explanation: ab − ba = 9(a − b), a multiple of 9.

questions.q: ab + ba is always divisible by ___ ?
questions.explanation: ab + ba = 11(a + b), a multiple of 11.
Digit sum 2 + 4 + 6 = 12, divisible by 3, so yes.

questions.q: A number 29 is reversed to 92. What is the difference?
If ab − ba = 36, then a − b = ___ ?
The sum of a two-digit number and its reverse is 88. What is a + b?
